facts.raw_span: A 28-year-old G2P1 woman presented 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
with worsening headache and easy fatigability for 3 days
The headache was continuous, global, and had become severe over 24 hours
associated with nausea and malaise
Eight days postoperatively she had developed a mild global headache managed with rest and paracetamol
By day 31 the headache was severe, nonpositional, and unrelieved by rest or analgesics
Vital signs were normal
She was fully conscious and oriented
all meningeal signs were negative
motor function was intact
Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count, prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, measuring 15 mm in width with a 13-mm midline shift

scope_out: no signs of increased intracranial pressure

scope_out: no signs of increased intracranial pressure

concepts.why: The noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection, which is consistent with a subdural hematoma, and the absence of meningeal signs suggests a subdural rather than subarachnoid location.

The CT findings of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection could also be consistent with an epidural hematoma, although the clinical context and absence of meningeal signs make this less likely.

The patient's worsening headache over 3 days and the presence of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on CT are consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma, which can present with gradual onset of symptoms.

rationales.F01: Elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia is a common procedure and does not specifically point to any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F02: Worsening headache is a nonspecific symptom that could be associated with any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F05: Development of a mild global headache postoperatively could be an early sign of a subdural or chronic subdural hematoma.
rationales.F06: Severe, nonpositional headache unrelieved by rest or analgesics suggests increased intracranial pressure, which could be due to a subdural or chronic subdural hematoma.
rationales.F09: Absence of meningeal signs makes conditions like meningitis less likely but does not strongly rule out subdural or epidural hematomas.
rationales.F12: The CT findings of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection are highly suggestive of a subdural hematoma, particularly a chronic one, and less likely an epidural hematoma due to the location and description.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's worsening headache and the presence of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on the CT scan, along with the timeline of 31 days post-cesarean, support the diagnosis of a chronic subdural hematoma.
